def qualify_cached_archive(archive,directory,name,version,expected):

        before=os.fstat(fd)
        require(stat.S_ISREG(before.st_mode) and 0<before.st_size<=32*1024*1024,'archive type/size outside bound')
        digest=hashlib.sha256();size=0
        while True:
            chunk=os.read(fd,65536)
            if not chunk:break
            size+=len(chunk);require(size<=32*1024*1024,'archive grew beyond bound');digest.update(chunk)
        archive_pin={'path':str(archive),'bytes':size,'sha256':digest.hexdigest(),'identity':identity(before)}
        require(size==before.st_size and digest.hexdigest()==expected,'existing archive checksum differs from original Cargo.lock')
        source_before=regular_tree(directory,4096,64*1024*1024)
        os.lseek(fd,0,os.SEEK_SET)

        with os.fdopen(os.dup(fd),'rb') as stream,tarfile.open(fileobj=stream,mode='r:gz') as packed:
            for member in packed:
                require(time.monotonic()<DEADLINE,'bounded registry observation deadline exhausted')
                if member.isdir() and member.name.rstrip('/')==name+'-'+version:
                    require('' not in directories,'duplicate archive root directory')
                    directories.add('');continue
                require(member.name.startswith(prefix) and not member.name.startswith('/'),'unexpected archive root')
                relative=member.name[len(prefix):]
                path=PurePosixPath(relative)
                require(relative and '..' not in path.parts and str(path)==relative.rstrip('/'),'noncanonical archive member')
                require(len(files)+len(directories)<4096,'archive member count exceeds bound')
                if member.isdir():
                    require(relative not in directories,'duplicate archive directory')
                    directories.add(relative);continue
                require(member.isfile() and relative not in files,'archive alias, special file or duplicate rejected')
                require(0<=member.size<=16*1024*1024 and total+member.size<=64*1024*1024,'archive expansion exceeds bound')
                reader=packed.extractfile(member);require(reader is not None,'archive regular member unreadable')
                member_hash=hashlib.sha256();member_size=0
                while True:
                    chunk=reader.read(65536)
                    if not chunk:break
                    member_size+=len(chunk);require(member_size<=member.size,'archive member exceeded declared size');member_hash.update(chunk)
                require(member_size==member.size,'archive member truncated')
                total+=member_size
                require(relative in source_before and source_before[relative]['bytes']==member_size and
                        source_before[relative]['sha256']==member_hash.hexdigest(),'extracted source differs from locked archive: '+str(directory/relative))

        extra={name:row for name,row in source_before.items() if name not in files}
        require(regular_tree(directory,4096,64*1024*1024)==source_before,'extracted source changed during archive comparison')
        require(identity(before)==identity(os.fstat(fd))==identity(archive.lstat()),'archive changed during comparison')

                'extra_files_are_only_cargo_marker':set(extra)<=set(['.cargo-ok']),
                'source_inventory':write_new(OUT/(name+'-'+version+'-source.json'),{'archive_files':files,'extras':extra}),
                'source_unchanged_after':True}
        require(set(extra)=={'.cargo-ok'} and extra['.cargo-ok']['bytes']==7 and
                extra['.cargo-ok']['sha256']=='afbf9d0f3560b0fd7795e81c42a0a79ee6b6fc67e064f77826aee642cad28d91',

class OwnChildReaper:
    """Retire only children of this single-threaded isolated controller."""
    def __init__(self):
        self.pid = os.getpid()
        self.original = None
        self.changed = False
        self.active = False
        self.record = {'pid': self.pid, 'begin_passed': False, 'restored': False,
                       'final_children_empty': False, 'max_adopted_per_command': 128,
                       'cleanup_seconds_per_command': 5}
        self.libc = ctypes.CDLL(None, use_errno=True)
        self.prctl = self.libc.prctl
        self.prctl.argtypes = [ctypes.c_int, ctypes.c_ulong, ctypes.c_ulong,
                              ctypes.c_ulong, ctypes.c_ulong]
        self.prctl.restype = ctypes.c_int

    def flag(self):
        value = ctypes.c_int(-1)
        if self.prctl(37, ctypes.addressof(value), 0, 0, 0) != 0:
            raise OSError(ctypes.get_errno(), 'PR_GET_CHILD_SUBREAPER')
        require(value.value in (0, 1), 'invalid own subreaper flag')
        return value.value

    def set_flag(self, value):
        if self.prctl(36, value, 0, 0, 0) != 0:
            raise OSError(ctypes.get_errno(), 'PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER')

    def single_thread(self):
        require(os.getpid() == self.pid and signal.getsignal(signal.SIGCHLD) == signal.SIG_DFL,
                'controller PID/SIGCHLD ownership changed')
        names = []
        with os.scandir('/proc/%d/task' % self.pid) as rows:
            for row in rows:
                names.append(row.name)
                require(len(names) <= 1, 'controller is no longer single-threaded')
        require(names == [str(self.pid)], 'controller thread identity changed')

    def children(self):
        # Fixed self task only, never an all-/proc or other-actor enumeration.
        fd = os.open('/proc/%d/task/%d/children' % (self.pid, self.pid),
                     os.O_RDONLY | os.O_CLOEXEC | os.O_NOFOLLOW)
        try:
            data = os.read(fd, 8193)
            require(len(data) <= 8192 and os.read(fd, 1) == b'', 'own children list exceeds bound')
        finally:
            os.close(fd)
        fields = data.split()
        require(len(fields) <= 128 and len(fields) == len(set(fields)), 'own child count differs')
        require(all(x.isdigit() and x == str(int(x)).encode() and 0 < int(x) < 2**31
                    for x in fields), 'malformed own children list')
        return [int(x) for x in fields]

    def empty(self):
        self.single_thread()
        require(self.children() == [], 'controller retains child processes')
        try:
            os.waitid(os.P_ALL, 0, os.WEXITED | os.WNOHANG | os.WNOWAIT)
        except ChildProcessError:
            return True
        raise RuntimeError('kernel wait authority did not confirm ECHILD')

    def begin(self):
        require(hasattr(os, 'P_PIDFD') and hasattr(os, 'WNOWAIT'), 'held nonreaping wait unavailable')
        self.empty()
        self.original = self.flag()
        self.record['original_subreaper_flag'] = self.original
        if self.original == 0:
            self.set_flag(1)
            self.changed = True
        require(self.flag() == 1, 'own subreaper did not become active')
        self.active = True
        self.record['begin_passed'] = True

    def before_command(self):
        require(self.active and self.flag() == 1, 'own subreaper not active')
        self.empty()

    def finish(self):
        self.empty()
        self.record['final_children_empty'] = True
        if self.original is not None:
            require(self.flag() == 1, 'own subreaper flag changed during commands')
            if self.changed:
                self.set_flag(self.original)
                self.changed = False
            require(self.flag() == self.original, 'own subreaper flag not restored')
        self.active = False
        self.record['restored'] = True

    @staticmethod
    def peek(pid, pidfd):
        info = os.waitid(os.P_PIDFD if pidfd is not None else os.P_PID,
                         pidfd if pidfd is not None else pid,
                         os.WEXITED | os.WNOHANG | os.WNOWAIT)
        if info is not None:
            require(info.si_pid == pid and info.si_code in
                    (os.CLD_EXITED, os.CLD_KILLED, os.CLD_DUMPED),
                    'owned child wait status differs')
        return info

    @staticmethod
    def observed(info):
        return {'pid': info.si_pid, 'code': info.si_code, 'status': info.si_status}

    def await_exit(self, pid, pidfd, deadline):
        poller = select.poll()
        poller.register(pidfd, select.POLLIN)
        while True:
            info = self.peek(pid, pidfd)
            if info is not None:
                return info
            remaining = deadline - time.monotonic()
            if remaining <= 0:
                raise TimeoutError('owned child exit deadline')
            poller.poll(max(1, min(100, int(remaining * 1000))))

    def retire(self, process, pidfd, record, remember, deadline):
        record['descendants'] = []
        record['owned_tree_cleanup_complete'] = False
        try:
            # WNOWAIT / direct-child relationship reserves the leader PID until
            # after group signalling. No killpg occurs after leader reaping.
            info = self.peek(process.pid, pidfd)
            record['leader_unreaped_before_group_cleanup'] = True
            record['leader_alive_before_group_cleanup'] = info is None
            if info is not None:
                record['leader_observed_before_reap'] = self.observed(info)
            require(os.getpgid(process.pid) == process.pid and
                    os.getsid(process.pid) == process.pid, 'owned session/group identity changed')
            record['owned_group_kill_attempted'] = True
            record['kill_attempted'] = True
            try:
                os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
                record['owned_group_kill_completed'] = True
            except ProcessLookupError:
                require(info is not None, 'live original group disappeared')
                record['owned_group_already_absent'] = True
        except Exception as error:
            remember(error, 'owned_group_cleanup')
            # If group qualification failed, kill only the known direct child.
            try:
                if self.peek(process.pid, pidfd) is None:
                    if pidfd is not None:
                        signal.pidfd_send_signal(pidfd, signal.SIGKILL)
                    else:
                        # The successful P_PID wait above proves this is still
                        # this controller's unreaped child, so its PID cannot be reused.
                        process.kill()
                    record['direct_child_fallback_kill_attempted'] = True
            except Exception as error:
                remember(error, 'direct_child_fallback_cleanup')
        try:
            process.wait(timeout=max(0, deadline - time.monotonic()))
            record['returncode'] = process.returncode
            record['child_reaped'] = True
        except Exception as error:
            remember(error, 'reap_direct_child')
        if not record['child_reaped']:
            return
        seen = set()
        while True:
            try:
                children = self.children()
                if not children:
                    self.empty()
                    record['owned_tree_cleanup_complete'] = True
                    break
                require(time.monotonic() < deadline, 'adopted child cleanup deadline')
                require(not (set(children) & seen), 'an earlier adopted child was not reaped')
                require(len(seen) + len(children) <= 128, 'adopted child total bound exceeded')
            except Exception as error:
                remember(error, 'adopted_child_list_or_gate')
                break
            complete = True
            for child in children:
                if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
                    remember(TimeoutError('adopted child cleanup deadline'), 'adopted_child_deadline')
                    complete = False
                    break
                seen.add(child)
                item = {'pid': child, 'kill_attempted': False, 'reaped': False, 'pidfd_closed': True}
                record['descendants'].append(item)
                held = None
                try:
                    # The kernel-listed unreaped direct/adopted child cannot be
                    # reaped by another waiter: this controller is single-threaded.
                    try:
                        held = os.pidfd_open(child, 0)
                        item['pidfd_closed'] = False
                    except Exception as error:
                        # Keep this failure, but still retire the kernel-proven
                        # unreaped child if descriptor allocation itself failed.
                        item['pidfd_open_error'] = repr(error)
                        remember(error, 'adopted_pidfd_open')
                    info = self.peek(child, held)
                    if info is None:
                        item['kill_attempted'] = True
                        if held is not None:
                            signal.pidfd_send_signal(held, signal.SIGKILL)
                            info = self.await_exit(child, held, deadline)
                        else:
                            os.kill(child, signal.SIGKILL)
                            while info is None and time.monotonic() < deadline:
                                time.sleep(0.005)
                                info = self.peek(child, None)
                            require(info is not None, 'owned child fallback wait deadline')
                    item['observed_before_reap'] = self.observed(info)
                    waited, status = os.waitpid(child, os.WNOHANG)
                    require(waited == child, 'observed terminal adopted child was not reaped')
                    item['wait_status'] = status
                    item['reaped'] = True
                except Exception as error:
                    complete = False
                    item['error'] = repr(error)
                    remember(error, 'adopted_child_cleanup')
                finally:
                    if held is not None:
                        value, held = held, None
                        try:
                            os.close(value)
                            item['pidfd_closed'] = True
                        except Exception as error:
                            complete = False
                            remember(error, 'adopted_pidfd_close')
            if not complete:
                break
        record['cleanup_elapsed_seconds'] = time.monotonic() - (deadline - 5)
        if record['descendants']:
            # Successful drivers must normally reap their own helpers. Cleanup
            # success is not permission to count orphaned/forced helpers as a
            # successful compilation.
            remember(RuntimeError('driver left descendant processes after its exit'),
                     'driver_left_descendants')



def owned_command(report, root, argv, timeout=25, pidfd_factory=None, environment=None, cwd=None, label=None):
    index = len(report['commands'])
    output = root / ('command%02d.stdout' % index)
    error_path = root / ('command%02d.stderr' % index)
    record = {'argv': argv, 'cwd': str(cwd or root), 'label': label, 'timeout_seconds': timeout,
              'timed_out': False, 'child_started': False, 'child_reaped': False,
              'kill_attempted': False, 'pidfd_closed': True, 'output_fds_closed': False,
              'first_error': None, 'secondary_errors': [],
              'owned_tree_cleanup_complete': False}
    report['commands'].append(record)
    process = None
    pidfd = None
    streams = []
    first = None

    def remember(error, stage):
        nonlocal first
        item = {'stage': stage, 'error': repr(error)}
        if first is None:
            first = error
            record['first_error'] = item
        else:
            record['secondary_errors'].append(item)

    try:
        CHILD_REAPER.before_command()
        remaining = DEADLINE - time.monotonic()
        require(remaining > 0, 'controller work deadline expired before child admission')
        for path in (output, error_path):
            streams.append(path.open('xb'))
        require(type(environment) is dict and environment.get('CARGO_NET_OFFLINE') == 'true',
                'fixed offline child environment missing')
        process = subprocess.Popen(argv, cwd=cwd or root, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            stdout=streams[0], stderr=streams[1], close_fds=True, start_new_session=True,
            preexec_fn=limit_child_outputs, env=environment)
        record['pid'] = process.pid
        record['child_started'] = True
        pidfd = (pidfd_factory or os.pidfd_open)(process.pid, 0)
        record['pidfd_closed'] = False
        try:
            info = CHILD_REAPER.await_exit(process.pid, pidfd,
                time.monotonic() + min(timeout, remaining))
            record['leader_observed_without_reap'] = CHILD_REAPER.observed(info)
            if info.si_code != os.CLD_EXITED or info.si_status != 0:
                remember(RuntimeError('original command exited unsuccessfully before cleanup'),
                         'leader_exit_status')
        except TimeoutError:
            record['timed_out'] = True
            raise subprocess.TimeoutExpired(argv, timeout)
    except Exception as error:
        remember(error, 'start_or_wait')
    finally:
        if process is not None:
            cleanup_deadline = time.monotonic() + 5
            try:
                CHILD_REAPER.retire(process, pidfd, record, remember, cleanup_deadline)
            except Exception as error:
                remember(error, 'unexpected_owned_tree_cleanup_error')
                # Do not let an unexpected diagnostic error skip the direct
                # child's final wait. Group/adoption qualification stays false.
                try:
                    if process.returncode is None and CHILD_REAPER.peek(process.pid, pidfd) is None:
                        if pidfd is not None:
                            signal.pidfd_send_signal(pidfd, signal.SIGKILL)
                        else:
                            process.kill()
                except Exception as error:
                    remember(error, 'final_direct_kill')
                try:
                    process.wait(timeout=max(0, cleanup_deadline - time.monotonic()))
                    record['returncode'] = process.returncode
                    record['child_reaped'] = True
                except Exception as error:
                    remember(error, 'final_direct_wait')
        if pidfd is not None:
            value, pidfd = pidfd, None
            try:
                os.close(value)
                record['pidfd_closed'] = True
            except Exception as error:
                remember(error, 'close_pidfd')
        closed = True
        for stream in reversed(streams):
            try:
                stream.close()
            except Exception as error:
                closed = False
                remember(error, 'close_output_file')
        record['output_fds_closed'] = closed
    # Each output is retained independently; a capture error cannot hide the
    # earlier child failure or prevent the other stream from being checked.

def run_child_lifecycle_controls(report, root, environment):
    control_root = root / 'host-child-lifecycle-controls'
    control_root.mkdir(mode=0o700)
    report['host_child_lifecycle_controls'] = []
    modes = ('timeout-descendant', 'escaped-descendant', 'pidfd-failure')
    for index, mode in enumerate(modes):
        case_root = control_root / ('case%02d' % index)
        case_root.mkdir(mode=0o700)
        case = {'name': mode, 'passed': False, 'commands': [],
                'Android_executed': False, 'namespace_or_UID_changes': False,
                'pidfd_failure_seam': mode == 'pidfd-failure'}
        report['host_child_lifecycle_controls'].append(case)
        first = None

        def denied_pidfd(pid, flags):
            raise OSError(errno.EMFILE, 'explicit owned-child pidfd-open control seam')

        try:
            owned_command(case, case_root,
                    [sys.executable, '-I', '-B', '-c', HOST_LIFECYCLE_FIXTURE, mode],
                    timeout=1 if mode == 'timeout-descendant' else 5,
                    pidfd_factory=denied_pidfd if mode == 'pidfd-failure' else None, environment=environment)
        except Exception as error:
            first = error
        require(first is not None and len(case['commands']) == 1,
                'lifecycle negative control unexpectedly succeeded')
        row = case['commands'][0]
        require(row['child_started'] and row['child_reaped'] and
                row['owned_tree_cleanup_complete'] and row['pidfd_closed'] and
                row['output_fds_closed'] and row.get('stdout_complete') and row.get('stderr_complete'),
                'lifecycle negative control did not completely retire its owned tree')
        require(row['stderr'] == '' and row['first_error'] is not None,
                'lifecycle negative control lost its first error or had unexpected stderr')
        if mode == 'pidfd-failure':
            require(isinstance(first, OSError) and first.errno == errno.EMFILE and
                    row['first_error']['stage'] == 'start_or_wait' and
                    row['returncode'] == -signal.SIGKILL and not row['descendants'],
                    'post-Popen pidfd failure did not preserve errno and reap the child')
        else:
            fields = row['stdout'].strip().split()
            require(len(fields) == 3 and fields[0] == 'READY' and
                    int(fields[1]) == row['pid'] and len(row['descendants']) == 1 and
                    row['descendants'][0]['pid'] == int(fields[2]) and
                    row['descendants'][0]['reaped'] and row['descendants'][0]['pidfd_closed'] and
                    os.WIFSIGNALED(row['descendants'][0]['wait_status']) and
                    os.WTERMSIG(row['descendants'][0]['wait_status']) == signal.SIGKILL,
                    'real descendant readiness/reaping proof differs')
            if mode == 'timeout-descendant':
                require(isinstance(first, subprocess.TimeoutExpired) and row['timed_out'] and
                        row['returncode'] == -signal.SIGKILL and
                        row['first_error']['stage'] == 'start_or_wait',
                        'timeout control did not retain the original failure')
            else:
                require(row['returncode'] == 0 and not row['timed_out'] and
                        row['descendants'][0]['kill_attempted'] and
                        row['first_error']['stage'] == 'driver_left_descendants',
                        'escaped descendant was not rejected and independently retired')
        CHILD_REAPER.empty()
        case['expected_failure'] = repr(first)
        case['passed'] = True
    require(len(report['host_child_lifecycle_controls']) == 3 and
            all(item['passed'] for item in report['host_child_lifecycle_controls']),
            'owned tree cleanup controls incomplete')

","candidate-control.rs":"//! Privileged two-phase Android task lifecycle service.

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
use std::sync::{Arc, Condvar, Mutex, MutexGuard};
use std::time::{Duration, SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};

use droidloom_composer::task_control::{TaskControlRegistry, TaskRegistration, TaskRegistrationPhase};
use droidloom_composer::{DisplayId, TaskId};
use droidloom_composer_aidl::denial::DenialPresentationSink;
use droidloom_composer_aidl::service::ComposerLifecycle;
use droidloom_denial_ipc::{SeqPacket, SeqPacketListener};
use droidloom_denial_protocol::TaskObjectId;
use droidloom_task_control::{
    decode_request, encode_response, ControlErrorCode, ControlRequest, ControlResponse,
    PROTOCOL_MAJOR, PROTOCOL_MINOR,
};

const AID_ROOT: u32 = 0;
const AID_SYSTEM: u32 = 1_000;
const CONFIGURE_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(5);

type ControlFailure = (ControlErrorCode, String);

#[derive(Debug)]
struct State {
    registry: TaskControlRegistry,
    retired: BTreeSet<TaskObjectId>,
    input_scales: BTreeMap<TaskObjectId, (u32, u32)>,
    direct_tasks: BTreeMap<TaskId, TaskObjectId>,
    direct_android_displays: BTreeMap<TaskObjectId, u32>,
    removals: BTreeMap<TaskObjectId, RemovalProgress>,
    endpoint_calls: BTreeMap<TaskObjectId, EndpointCalls>,
}

/// Calls made for one never-reused object/display. Record each invocation
/// before crossing the backend boundary: Err cannot prove it had no effects.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
struct EndpointCalls {
    display: DisplayId,
    composer: bool,
    denial: bool,
}

/// Retirement completion for this exact object/display. An endpoint is
/// complete only if it was never invoked or its cleanup returned Ok.
/// An error never upgrades either fact.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
struct RemovalProgress {
    display: DisplayId,
    denial_complete: bool,
    composer_complete: bool,
}

struct DirectReservation {
    object: TaskObjectId,
    display: DisplayId,
    task: TaskId,
    android_display: u32,
    package: String,
}

impl DirectReservation {
    fn matches(&self, state: &State, registration: &TaskRegistration) -> bool {
        registration.object == self.object
            && registration.reservation.display == self.display
            && registration.reservation.package == self.package
            && state.direct_tasks.get(&self.task) == Some(&self.object)
            && state.direct_android_displays.get(&self.object) == Some(&self.android_display)
    }
}

/// Cloneable coordinator shared by the control listener and Denial event pump.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct TaskCoordinator {
    sink: DenialPresentationSink,
    lifecycle: ComposerLifecycle,
    state: Arc<(Mutex<State>, Condvar)>,
    operation_gate: Arc<Mutex<()>>,
    direct_registration_gate: Arc<Mutex<()>>,
}

impl TaskCoordinator {
    /// Create an empty coordinator for one Composer/Denial connection.
    pub fn new(sink: DenialPresentationSink, lifecycle: ComposerLifecycle) -> Self {
        let first_object = SystemTime::now()
            .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
            .ok()
            .and_then(|elapsed| u64::try_from(elapsed.as_nanos()).ok())
            .filter(|object| *object <= i64::MAX as u64)
            .unwrap_or(1);
        Self {
            sink,
            lifecycle,
            state: Arc::new((
                Mutex::new(State {
                    registry: TaskControlRegistry::with_first_ids(1, first_object)
                        .expect("wall-clock object seed is a positive signed 64-bit value"),
                    retired: BTreeSet::new(),
                    input_scales: BTreeMap::new(),
                    direct_tasks: BTreeMap::new(),
                    direct_android_displays: BTreeMap::new(),
                    removals: BTreeMap::new(),
                    endpoint_calls: BTreeMap::new(),
                }),
                Condvar::new(),
            )),
            operation_gate: Arc::new(Mutex::new(())),
            direct_registration_gate: Arc::new(Mutex::new(())),
        }
    }

    /// Create the configured default display SurfaceFlinger requires before
    /// Android's activity services are available. This display is deliberately
    /// left unbound: later application launches still reserve independent
    /// display/window identities through the task-control protocol.
    pub fn stage_bootstrap_display(
        &self,
        package: String,
    ) -> Result<(TaskObjectId, DisplayId), String> {
        match self.reserve(0, package).map_err(|(code, message)| {
            format!("bootstrap display reservation failed ({code:?}): {message}")
        })? {
            ControlResponse::Reserved {
                object, display, ..
            } => Ok((TaskObjectId(object), DisplayId(display))),
            _ => Err("bootstrap display reservation returned an unexpected response".to_owned()),
        }
    }

    /// Mark the first configured display as launchable and wake its pending
    /// reserve request. Later reconfigures leave the bound phase unchanged.
    pub fn display_connected(&self, object: TaskObjectId) -> Result<(), String> {
        let (state, changed) = &*self.state;
        let mut state = state
            .lock()
            .map_err(|_| "task-control state lock is poisoned".to_owned())?;
        let phase = state
            .registry
            .get(object)
            .map_err(|error| error.to_string())?
            .phase;
        if phase == TaskRegistrationPhase::Staged {
            state
                .registry
                .mark_connected(object)
                .map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
            changed.notify_all();
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Record the logical-to-buffer scale carried by the latest configure.
    pub fn set_input_scale(
        &self,
        object: TaskObjectId,
        numerator: u32,
        denominator: u32,
    ) -> Result<(), String> {
        if numerator == 0 || denominator == 0 {
            return Err(format!(
                "Droidloom object {} received an invalid input scale {numerator}/{denominator}",
                object.0
            ));
        }
        let mut state = self
            .state
            .0
            .lock()
            .map_err(|_| "task-control state lock is poisoned".to_owned())?;
        state
            .registry
            .get(object)
            .map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
        state.input_scales.insert(object, (numerator, denominator));
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Return whether an object was intentionally removed, allowing the event
    /// pump to discard an already-queued final event without accepting random
    /// unknown object identities.
    pub fn is_retired(&self, object: TaskObjectId) -> bool {
        self.state
            .0
            .lock()
            .map(|state| state.retired.contains(&object))
            .unwrap_or(false)
    }

    /// Return whether this object is a SurfaceFlinger-owned task channel and
    /// therefore must never be advertised as an Android logical display.
    pub fn is_direct_task(&self, object: TaskObjectId) -> bool {
        self.state
            .0
            .lock()
            .map(|state| state.direct_android_displays.contains_key(&object))
            .unwrap_or(false)
    }

    /// Register one launcher- or observer-verified WindowManager task for direct export.
    /// The channel reuses safe Composer window state but intentionally skips
    /// Composer hotplug: it is not an Android display. This explicit registry
    /// is also the allowlist that excludes HOME and system organizer tasks.
    pub fn register_direct_task(
        &self,
        task: TaskId,
        package: String,
        android_display: u32,
    ) -> Result<(TaskObjectId, DisplayId), String> {
        // Lock order is registration -> operation -> state. Do not hold the
        // operation/state guards while reserve waits for the configure event.
        let _registration = self.direct_registration_gate.lock()
            .map_err(|_| "direct registration lock is poisoned".to_owned())?;
        if task.0 == 0 || task.0 > i32::MAX as u64 {
            return Err(format!("invalid Android task identity {}", task.0));
        }
        {
            let _operation = self.operation_gate.lock()
                .map_err(|_| "task-control operation lock is poisoned".to_owned())?;
            let state = self.state.0.lock()
                .map_err(|_| "task-control state lock is poisoned".to_owned())?;
            if let Some(existing) = state.direct_tasks.get(&task).copied() {
                let registration = state.registry.get(existing)
                    .map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
                if registration.reservation.package != package
                    || state.direct_android_displays.get(&existing) != Some(&android_display)
                {
                    return Err(format!(
                        "Android task {} is already registered with different ownership",
                        task.0
                    ));
                }
                // A Removing entry still carries its old task/display fields.
                // Those fields alone must never qualify it for reuse.
                if registration.phase != TaskRegistrationPhase::Bound
                    || registration.task != Some(task)
                    || registration.android_display != Some(android_display)
                    || state.removals.contains_key(&existing)
                    || state.endpoint_calls.get(&existing) != Some(&EndpointCalls {
                        display: registration.reservation.display,
                        composer: true,
                        denial: true,
                    })
                {
                    return Err(format!(
                        "Android task {} direct registration is not fully Bound ({:?})",
                        task.0, registration.phase
                    ));
                }
                return Ok((existing, registration.reservation.display));
            }
        }

        let response = self
            .reserve_with_kind(0, package.clone(), Some((task, android_display)))
            .map_err(|(code, message)| {
                format!("direct task reserve failed ({code:?}): {message}")
            })?;
        let ControlResponse::Reserved { object, display, .. } = response else {
            return Err("direct task reservation returned an unexpected response".to_owned());
        };
        let reservation = DirectReservation {
            object: TaskObjectId(object),
            display: DisplayId(display),
            task,
            android_display,
            package,
        };
        let operation = self.operation_gate.lock().map_err(|_| {
            format!("task-control operation lock is poisoned after reserving direct object {}; cleanup is unqualified",
                    reservation.object.0)
        })?;
        let binding: Result<(), String> = (|| {
            // A retire request may have run during the configure wait. Recheck
            // this exact reservation under the same gate as binding/teardown.
            let already_bound = {
                let state = self.state.0.lock()
                    .map_err(|_| "task-control state lock is poisoned".to_owned())?;
                let registration = state.registry.get(reservation.object)
                    .map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
                if !reservation.matches(&state, registration)
                    || state.endpoint_calls.get(&reservation.object) != Some(&EndpointCalls {
                        display: reservation.display,
                        composer: true,
                        denial: true,
                    })
                {
                    return Err("direct reservation ownership or endpoint calls changed before binding".to_owned());
                }
                if registration.phase == TaskRegistrationPhase::Bound
                    && registration.task == Some(task)
                    && registration.android_display == Some(android_display)
                    && !state.removals.contains_key(&reservation.object)
                {
                    true
                } else if registration.phase == TaskRegistrationPhase::Connected
                    && registration.task.is_none()
                    && registration.android_display.is_none()
                    && !state.removals.contains_key(&reservation.object)
                {
                    false
                } else {
                    return Err(format!(
                        "direct object {} is not awaiting complete binding ({:?})",
                        reservation.object.0, registration.phase
                    ));
                }
            };
            if already_bound {
                return Ok(());
            }
            self.sink.bind_task(reservation.display, task)
                .map_err(|error| format!("bind direct Denial task identity: {error}"))?;
            self.lifecycle.bind_direct_task(reservation.display, task)
                .map_err(|error| format!("bind direct Composer task identity: {error:?}"))?;
            // Return an owned Result from this scope. Its state guard is gone
            // before a failure reaches rollback, which locks state itself.
            let result = {
                let mut state = self.state.0.lock()
                    .map_err(|_| "task-control state lock is poisoned".to_owned())?;
                let registration = state.registry.get(reservation.object)
                    .map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
                if !reservation.matches(&state, registration) {
                    return Err("direct reservation ownership changed before registry commit".to_owned());
                }
                state.registry.bind_task(reservation.object, task, android_display)
                    .map(|_| ())
                    .map_err(|error| error.to_string())
            };
            result
        })();
        if let Err(primary) = binding {
            return match self.rollback_direct_locked(&reservation, &operation) {
                Ok(()) => Err(primary),
                Err((code, cleanup)) => Err(format!(
                    "{primary}; cleanup of direct object {} failed ({code:?}): {cleanup}",
                    reservation.object.0
                )),
            };
        }
        Ok((reservation.object, reservation.display))
    }

    fn rollback_direct_locked(
        &self,
        reservation: &DirectReservation,
        operation: &MutexGuard<'_, ()>,
    ) -> Result<(), ControlFailure> {
        {
            let state = self.state.0.lock()
                .map_err(|_| backend("task-control state lock is poisoned"))?;
            if !state.retired.contains(&reservation.object) {
                let registration = state.registry.get(reservation.object)
                    .map_err(control_error)?;
                if !reservation.matches(&state, registration) {
                    return Err((ControlErrorCode::Conflict,
                        "refusing cleanup of a changed direct reservation".to_owned()));
                }
                if registration.phase == TaskRegistrationPhase::Bound {
                    return Err((ControlErrorCode::Conflict,
                        "refusing rollback of a complete Bound direct registration".to_owned()));
                }
            }
        }
        // This gate is already held. Calling remove()/retire_direct_task()
        // here would recursively lock it; remove_internal_locked never does.
        self.remove_internal_locked(reservation.object, operation)
    }

    /// Resolve a previously authorized direct task without creating anything.
    /// SurfaceFlinger connections for HOME or other unsolicited tasks fail
    /// closed here and therefore never create a Denial window.
    pub fn direct_task_display(&self, task: TaskId) -> Result<DisplayId, String> {
        let state = self
            .state
            .0
            .lock()
            .map_err(|_| "task-control state lock is poisoned".to_owned())?;
        let object = state
            .direct_tasks
            .get(&task)
            .copied()
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("Android task {} is not authorized for export", task.0))?;

            .registry
            .get(object)
            .map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;

        }

    }

    /// Remove exactly one direct task after SurfaceFlinger observes that

    pub fn retire_direct_task(&self, task: TaskId) -> Result<(), String> {
        let _operation = self
            .operation_gate
            .lock()
            .map_err(|_| "task-control operation lock is poisoned".to_owned())?;

            .state

            .get(&task)

    /// Accept authenticated privileged clients forever. Each connection is
    /// independent so a configure wait cannot block teardown/status traffic.
    pub fn serve(&self, listener: SeqPacketListener) -> Result<(), String> {
        loop {
            let socket = listener
                .accept()
                .map_err(|error| format!("accept task-control client: {error}"))?;
            let credentials = socket
                .peer_credentials()
                .map_err(|error| format!("authenticate task-control client: {error}"))?;
            if credentials.uid != AID_ROOT && credentials.uid != AID_SYSTEM {
                eprintln!(
                    "Droidloom rejected task-control peer pid={} uid={} gid={}",
                    credentials.pid, credentials.uid, credentials.gid
                );
                continue;
            }
            let coordinator = self.clone();
            std::thread::Builder::new()
                .name("droidloom-task-client".to_owned())
                .spawn(move || {
                    if let Err(error) = coordinator.serve_connection(&socket) {
                        eprintln!("Droidloom task-control client closed: {error}");
                    }
                })
                .map_err(|error| format!("start task-control client thread: {error}"))?;
        }
    }

    fn serve_connection(&self, socket: &SeqPacket) -> Result<(), String> {
        let mut ready = false;
        loop {
            let record = socket
                .receive_record()
                .map_err(|error| format!("receive task-control record: {error}"))?;
            if !record.descriptors.is_empty() {
                return Err("task-control record carried forbidden descriptors".to_owned());
            }
            let request = decode_request(&record.bytes)
                .map_err(|error| format!("decode task-control record: {error}"))?;
            let response = match request {
                ControlRequest::Hello {
                    min_major,
                    max_major,
                } if !ready && min_major <= PROTOCOL_MAJOR && max_major >= PROTOCOL_MAJOR => {
                    ready = true;
                    ControlResponse::ServerHello {
                        major: PROTOCOL_MAJOR,
                        minor: PROTOCOL_MINOR,
                    }
                }
                ControlRequest::Hello { .. } => error_response(
                    0,
                    ControlErrorCode::Protocol,
                    "repeated or incompatible task-control hello".to_owned(),
                ),
                request if !ready => error_response(
                    request_id(&request),
                    ControlErrorCode::Protocol,
                    "task-control hello is required".to_owned(),
                ),
                request => {
                    let request_id = request_id(&request);
                    match self.handle(request) {
                        Ok(response) => response,
                        Err((code, message)) => error_response(request_id, code, message),
                    }
                }
            };
            let bytes = encode_response(&response)
                .map_err(|error| format!("encode task-control response: {error}"))?;
            socket
                .send_record(&bytes, &[])
                .map_err(|error| format!("send task-control response: {error}"))?;
        }
    }

    fn handle(&self, request: ControlRequest) -> Result<ControlResponse, ControlFailure> {
        match request {
            ControlRequest::Reserve {
                request_id,
                package,
            } => self.reserve(request_id, package),
            ControlRequest::Bind {
                request_id,
                object,
                task,
                android_display,
            } => self.bind(
                request_id,
                TaskObjectId(object),
                TaskId(task),
                android_display,
            ),
            ControlRequest::RegisterDirect {
                request_id,
                package,
                task,
                android_display,
            } => self.register_direct(request_id, package, TaskId(task), android_display),
            ControlRequest::Remove { request_id, object } => {
                self.remove(request_id, TaskObjectId(object))
            }
            ControlRequest::Hello { .. } => Err((
                ControlErrorCode::Protocol,
                "unexpected hello dispatch".to_owned(),
            )),
        }
    }

    fn reserve(&self, request_id: u64, package: String) -> Result<ControlResponse, ControlFailure> {
        self.reserve_with_kind(request_id, package, None)
    }

    fn register_direct(
        &self,
        request_id: u64,
        package: String,
        task: TaskId,
        android_display: u32,
    ) -> Result<ControlResponse, ControlFailure> {
        if android_display > i32::MAX as u32 {
            return Err((
                ControlErrorCode::InvalidRequest,
                format!("Android display ID {android_display} exceeds the framework range"),
            ));
        }
        let (object, display) = self
            .register_direct_task(task, package, android_display)
            .map_err(backend)?;
        self.sink.request_activation(display).map_err(|error| backend(error.to_string()))?;
        Ok(ControlResponse::Bound {
            request_id,
            object: object.0,
            task: task.0,
            display: display.0,
            android_display,
        })
    }

    fn reserve_with_kind(
        &self,
        request_id: u64,
        package: String,
        direct_task: Option<(TaskId, u32)>,
    ) -> Result<ControlResponse, ControlFailure> {
        let registration = {
            let operation = self.operation_gate.lock()
                .map_err(|_| backend("task-control operation lock is poisoned"))?;
            let registration = {
                let mut state = self.state.0.lock()
                    .map_err(|_| backend("task-control state lock is poisoned"))?;

                        return Err((ControlErrorCode::Conflict,
                            format!("Android task {} already has a direct channel", task.0)));
                    }
                }
                let registration = state.registry.reserve(package).map_err(control_error)?;

                    display: registration.reservation.display,
                    composer: false,
                    denial: false,
                });

                    state.direct_tasks.insert(task, registration.object);
                    state.direct_android_displays.insert(registration.object, android_display);

            };

                        .map_err(|_| backend("task-control state lock is poisoned"))?;

            .lock()

            .wait_timeout_while(state, CONFIGURE_TIMEOUT, |state| {

                    .registry
                    .get(registration.object)
                    .is_ok_and(|current| current.phase == TaskRegistrationPhase::Staged)

            .registry

                registration.object.0,

                Ok(()) => primary,
                Err((code, cleanup)) => format!(
                    "{primary}; reservation cleanup failed ({code:?}): {cleanup}"
                ),

        }
        Ok(ControlResponse::Reserved {
            request_id,
            object: registration.object.0,
            display: registration.reservation.display.0,

    }

    fn bind(
        &self,
        request_id: u64,
        object: TaskObjectId,
        task: TaskId,
        android_display: u32,
    ) -> Result<ControlResponse, ControlFailure> {
        if android_display > i32::MAX as u32 {
            return Err((
                ControlErrorCode::InvalidRequest,
                format!("Android display ID {android_display} exceeds the framework range"),
            ));
        }
        let _operation = self
            .operation_gate
            .lock()
            .map_err(|_| backend("task-control operation lock is poisoned"))?;
        let registration = {
            let state = self
                .state
                .0
                .lock()
                .map_err(|_| backend("task-control state lock is poisoned"))?;
            let registration = state.registry.get(object).map_err(control_error)?.clone();
            if registration.phase == TaskRegistrationPhase::Bound
                && registration.task == Some(task)
                && registration.android_display == Some(android_display)
            {
                return Ok(ControlResponse::Bound {
                    request_id,
                    object: object.0,
                    task: task.0,
                    display: registration.reservation.display.0,
                    android_display,
                });
            }
            if registration.phase != TaskRegistrationPhase::Connected {
                return Err((
                    ControlErrorCode::Conflict,
                    format!("object {} is not awaiting task binding", object.0),
                ));
            }
            registration
        };
        self.sink
            .bind_task(registration.reservation.display, task)
            .map_err(|error| backend(format!("bind Denial task identity: {error}")))?;
        self.lifecycle
            .bind_task(registration.reservation.display, task)
            .map_err(|error| backend(format!("bind Composer task identity: {error:?}")))?;
        let spec = self
            .state
            .0
            .lock()
            .map_err(|_| backend("task-control state lock is poisoned"))?
            .registry
            .bind_task(object, task, android_display)
            .map_err(control_error)?;
        Ok(ControlResponse::Bound {
            request_id,
            object: object.0,
            task: task.0,
            display: spec.display.0,
            android_display,
        })
    }

    /// Resolve the Android task, display, and logical-to-buffer scale for a live object.
    pub fn input_route_for_object(
        &self,
        object: TaskObjectId,
    ) -> Result<(TaskId, u32, u32, u32), String> {
        let state = self
            .state
            .0
            .lock()
            .map_err(|_| "task-control state lock is poisoned".to_owned())?;
        let registration = state
            .registry
            .get(object)
            .map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
        let android_display = registration.android_display.ok_or_else(|| {
            format!(
                "Droidloom object {} has not been bound to an Android logical display",
                object.0
            )
        })?;
        let task = registration.task.ok_or_else(|| {
            format!(
                "Droidloom object {} has not been bound to an Android task",
                object.0
            )
        })?;
        let (numerator, denominator) =
            state.input_scales.get(&object).copied().ok_or_else(|| {
                format!(
                    "Droidloom object {} has not received a configured input scale",
                    object.0
                )
            })?;
        Ok((task, android_display, numerator, denominator))
    }

    /// Resolve the real Android task behind an explicitly authorized direct object.
    pub fn direct_task_route_for_object(
        &self,
        object: TaskObjectId,
    ) -> Result<(TaskId, u32), String> {
        let state = self
            .state
            .0
            .lock()
            .map_err(|_| "task-control state lock is poisoned".to_owned())?;
        let android_display = state
            .direct_android_displays
            .get(&object)
            .copied()
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("Droidloom object {} is not a direct task", object.0))?;
        let task = state
            .direct_tasks
            .iter()
            .find_map(|(task, owned_object)| (*owned_object == object).then_some(*task))
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("Droidloom object {} has no Android task", object.0))?;
        Ok((task, android_display))
    }

    fn remove(
        &self,
        request_id: u64,
        object: TaskObjectId,
    ) -> Result<ControlResponse, ControlFailure> {
        let operation = self.operation_gate.lock()
            .map_err(|_| backend("task-control operation lock is poisoned"))?;
        self.remove_internal_locked(object, &operation)?;
        Ok(ControlResponse::Removed {
            request_id,
            object: object.0,
        })
    }

    fn remove_internal(&self, object: TaskObjectId) -> Result<(), ControlFailure> {
        let operation = self.operation_gate.lock()
            .map_err(|_| backend("task-control operation lock is poisoned"))?;
        self.remove_internal_locked(object, &operation)
    }

    fn forget_direct_object(state: &mut State, object: TaskObjectId) {
        state.direct_android_displays.remove(&object);
        state.direct_tasks.retain(|_, owned_object| *owned_object != object);
    }

    fn record_endpoint_call_locked(
        &self,
        object: TaskObjectId,
        display: DisplayId,
        denial: bool,
        _operation: &MutexGuard<'_, ()>,
    ) -> Result<(), ControlFailure> {
        let mut state = self.state.0.lock()
            .map_err(|_| backend("task-control state lock is poisoned"))?;
        let registration = state.registry.get(object).map_err(control_error)?;
        let expected_phase = if denial {
            TaskRegistrationPhase::Staged
        } else {
            TaskRegistrationPhase::Reserved
        };
        if registration.phase != expected_phase
            || registration.reservation.display != display
            || state.removals.contains_key(&object)
        {
            return Err((ControlErrorCode::Conflict,
                "endpoint invocation is not for this pending reservation".to_owned()));
        }
        let calls = state.endpoint_calls.get_mut(&object).ok_or_else(|| {
            backend("reservation endpoint-call record is missing")
        })?;
        if calls.display != display || calls.denial || (calls.composer != denial) {
            return Err((ControlErrorCode::Conflict,
                "reservation endpoint invocation order changed".to_owned()));
        }
        if denial {
            calls.denial = true;
        } else {
            calls.composer = true;
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn record_removal_locked(
        &self,
        object: TaskObjectId,
        progress: RemovalProgress,
        _operation: &MutexGuard<'_, ()>,
    ) -> Result<(), ControlFailure> {
        let mut state = self.state.0.lock()
            .map_err(|_| backend("task-control state lock is poisoned"))?;
        let registration = state.registry.get(object).map_err(control_error)?;
        let previous = state.removals.get(&object).copied().ok_or_else(|| {
            backend("task retirement progress is missing")
        })?;
        if !matches!(registration.phase,
                TaskRegistrationPhase::Reserved | TaskRegistrationPhase::Removing)
            || registration.reservation.display != progress.display
            || previous.display != progress.display
            || (previous.denial_complete && !progress.denial_complete)
            || (previous.composer_complete && !progress.composer_complete)
            || (progress.composer_complete && !progress.denial_complete)
        {
            return Err((ControlErrorCode::Conflict,
                "task retirement identity or progress changed".to_owned()));
        }
        state.removals.insert(object, progress);
        Ok(())
    }

    fn remove_internal_locked(
        &self,
        object: TaskObjectId,
        operation: &MutexGuard<'_, ()>,
    ) -> Result<(), ControlFailure> {
        let (registration, mut progress) = {
            let mut state = self.state.0.lock()
                .map_err(|_| backend("task-control state lock is poisoned"))?;
            if state.retired.contains(&object) {
                if state.registry.get(object).is_ok()
                    || state.direct_android_displays.contains_key(&object)
                    || state.direct_tasks.values().any(|owned| *owned == object)
                    || state.input_scales.contains_key(&object)
                    || state.removals.contains_key(&object)
                    || state.endpoint_calls.contains_key(&object)
                {
                    return Err((ControlErrorCode::Conflict,
                        "retired object still has live coordinator state".to_owned()));
                }
                return Ok(());
            }
            let registration = state.registry.get(object).map_err(control_error)?.clone();
            let calls = state.endpoint_calls.get(&object).copied().ok_or_else(|| {
                backend("reservation endpoint-call record is missing")
            })?;
            if calls.display != registration.reservation.display
                || (calls.denial && !calls.composer)
            {
                return Err((ControlErrorCode::Conflict,
                    "reservation endpoint calls are not for this display".to_owned()));
            }
            if registration.phase != TaskRegistrationPhase::Reserved
                && registration.phase != TaskRegistrationPhase::Removing
            {
                state.registry.begin_removal(object).map_err(control_error)?;
            }
            let progress = *state.removals.entry(object).or_insert(RemovalProgress {
                display: registration.reservation.display,
                denial_complete: !calls.denial,
                composer_complete: !calls.composer,
            });
            if progress.display != registration.reservation.display
                || (!calls.denial && !progress.denial_complete)
                || (!calls.composer && !progress.composer_complete)
                || (progress.composer_complete && !progress.denial_complete)
            {
                return Err((ControlErrorCode::Conflict,
                    "task retirement progress is not for this display".to_owned()));
            }
            (registration, progress)
        };

        // A Reserved entry can already have an attempted Composer call. It
        // must not be cancelled until every invoked endpoint is qualified.
        // Denial register Err may leave no local channel: UnknownDisplay then
        // remains an unresolved cleanup error, never evidence of remote absence.
        // Preserve ordering and each completed step. If Composer fails after
        // Denial succeeds, a later explicit retirement skips Denial; it must
        // not get stuck on the now-absent Denial channel. UnknownDisplay and
        // BadDisplay are never treated as successful cleanup.
        if !progress.denial_complete {
            self.sink.unregister_task(registration.reservation.display)
                .map_err(|error| backend(format!("destroy Denial task: {error}")))?;
            progress.denial_complete = true;
            self.record_removal_locked(object, progress, operation)?;
        }
        if !progress.composer_complete {
            self.lifecycle.remove_display(registration.reservation.display)
                .map_err(|error| backend(format!("remove Composer display: {error:?}")))?;
            progress.composer_complete = true;
            self.record_removal_locked(object, progress, operation)?;
        }
        let mut state = self.state.0.lock()
            .map_err(|_| backend("task-control state lock is poisoned"))?;
        if state.removals.get(&object) != Some(&progress)
            || !progress.denial_complete || !progress.composer_complete
        {
            return Err((ControlErrorCode::Conflict,
                "both backend retirement successes were not retained".to_owned()));
        }
        let phase = state.registry.get(object).map_err(control_error)?.phase;
        if phase == TaskRegistrationPhase::Reserved {
            state.registry.cancel_reservation(object).map_err(control_error)?;
        } else {
            state.registry.finish_removal(object).map_err(control_error)?;
        }
        state.input_scales.remove(&object);
        Self::forget_direct_object(&mut state, object);
        state.removals.remove(&object);
        state.endpoint_calls.remove(&object);
        state.retired.insert(object);
        self.state.1.notify_all();
        Ok(())
    }
}

fn request_id(request: &ControlRequest) -> u64 {
    match request {
        ControlRequest::Hello { .. } => 0,
        ControlRequest::Reserve { request_id, .. }
        | ControlRequest::Bind { request_id, .. }
        | ControlRequest::RegisterDirect { request_id, .. }
        | ControlRequest::Remove { request_id, .. } => *request_id,
    }
}

fn control_error(error: impl std::fmt::Display) -> ControlFailure {
    let message = error.to_string();
    let code = if message.contains("no registration") || message.contains("no native") {
        ControlErrorCode::NotFound
    } else if message.contains("already") || message.contains("cannot move") {
        ControlErrorCode::Conflict
    } else {
        ControlErrorCode::InvalidRequest
    };
    (code, message)
}

fn backend(message: impl Into<String>) -> ControlFailure {
    (ControlErrorCode::Backend, message.into())
}

fn error_response(request_id: u64, code: ControlErrorCode, message: String) -> ControlResponse {
    let mut bounded = String::with_capacity(message.len().min(1_024));
    for character in message.chars() {
        if bounded.len() + character.len_utf8() > 1_024 {
            break;
        }
        bounded.push(character);
    }
    if bounded.is_empty() {
        bounded.push_str("unspecified task-control failure");
    }
    ControlResponse::Error {
        request_id,
        code,
        message: bounded,
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq, Ord, PartialOrd)]
pub enum Point { Stage, Register, SinkBind, ComposerBind, Destroy, Remove, Activate }

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum Moment { Before, After }

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub enum Fault { Before(&'static str), After(&'static str) }

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct FixtureError(&'static str);
impl std::fmt::Display for FixtureError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result { f.write_str(self.0) }
}
impl std::error::Error for FixtureError {}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
struct Window { package: String, task: Option<TaskId> }
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
struct Channel { object: TaskObjectId, task: Option<TaskId> }

#[derive(Default)]
struct Data {
    windows: BTreeMap<DisplayId, Window>,
    channels: BTreeMap<DisplayId, Channel>,
    calls: Vec<(Point, DisplayId)>,
    faults: BTreeMap<Point, VecDeque<Fault>>,
}
type Observer = Arc<dyn Fn(Point, Moment, DisplayId) + Send + Sync>;
type Configure = Arc<dyn Fn(TaskObjectId) + Send + Sync>;

#[derive(Clone, Default)]
pub struct Backend {
    data: Arc<Mutex<Data>>,
    observer: Arc<Mutex<Option<Observer>>>,
    configure: Arc<Mutex<Option<Configure>>>,
}
impl Backend {
    pub fn fail(&self, point: Point, fault: Fault) {
        self.data.lock().unwrap().faults.entry(point).or_default().push_back(fault);
    }
    pub fn observe(&self, observer: Observer) {
        *self.observer.lock().unwrap() = Some(observer);
    }
    pub fn configure_with(&self, configure: Option<Configure>) {
        *self.configure.lock().unwrap() = configure;
    }
    fn notify(&self, point: Point, moment: Moment, display: DisplayId) {
        let callback = self.observer.lock().unwrap().clone();
        if let Some(callback) = callback { callback(point, moment, display); }
    }
    fn perform<T>(
        &self,
        point: Point,
        display: DisplayId,
        change: impl FnOnce(&mut Data) -> Result<T, FixtureError>,
    ) -> Result<T, FixtureError> {
        self.notify(point, Moment::Before, display);
        let (result, effect_applied) = {
            let mut data = self.data.lock().unwrap();
            data.calls.push((point, display));
            let fault = data.faults.entry(point).or_default().pop_front();
            if let Some(Fault::Before(message)) = fault {
                (Err(FixtureError(message)), false)
            } else {
                match change(&mut data) {
                    Err(error) => (Err(error), false),
                    Ok(value) => (
                        match fault {
                            Some(Fault::After(message)) => Err(FixtureError(message)),
                            _ => Ok(value),
                        },
                        true,
                    ),
                }
            }
        };
        // No fixture mutex is held while production callbacks run.
        if effect_applied { self.notify(point, Moment::After, display); }
        result
    }
    pub fn calls(&self) -> Vec<(Point, DisplayId)> { self.data.lock().unwrap().calls.clone() }
    pub fn count(&self, point: Point) -> usize {
        self.data.lock().unwrap().calls.iter().filter(|(p, _)| *p == point).count()
    }
    pub fn endpoints_empty(&self) -> bool {
        let data = self.data.lock().unwrap();
        data.windows.is_empty() && data.channels.is_empty()
    }
    pub fn has_window(&self, display: DisplayId) -> bool {
        self.data.lock().unwrap().windows.contains_key(&display)
    }
    pub fn has_channel(&self, display: DisplayId) -> bool {
        self.data.lock().unwrap().channels.contains_key(&display)
    }
    pub fn bound_tasks(&self, display: DisplayId) -> (Option<TaskId>, Option<TaskId>) {
        let data = self.data.lock().unwrap();
        (data.channels.get(&display).and_then(|v| v.task),
         data.windows.get(&display).and_then(|v| v.task))
    }
}

pub mod denial {
    use super::*;
    #[derive(Clone)]
    pub struct DenialPresentationSink { backend: Backend }
    impl DenialPresentationSink {
        pub fn fixture(backend: Backend) -> Self { Self { backend } }
        pub fn register_task(
            &self, object: TaskObjectId, reservation: &ReservedTaskWindowSpec,
        ) -> Result<(), FixtureError> {
            self.backend.perform(Point::Register, reservation.display, |data| {
                if !data.windows.contains_key(&reservation.display) {
                    return Err(FixtureError("composer-not-staged"));
                }
                if data.channels.contains_key(&reservation.display)
                    || data.channels.values().any(|v| v.object == object)
                {
                    return Err(FixtureError("duplicate-channel"));
                }
                data.channels.insert(reservation.display, Channel { object, task: None });
                Ok(())
            })?;
            let configure = self.backend.configure.lock().unwrap().clone();
            if let Some(configure) = configure { configure(object); }
            Ok(())
        }
        pub fn bind_task(&self, display: DisplayId, task: TaskId) -> Result<(), FixtureError> {
            self.backend.perform(Point::SinkBind, display, |data| {
                if data.channels.iter().any(|(id, value)| *id != display && value.task == Some(task)) {
                    return Err(FixtureError("duplicate-channel-task"));
                }
                let channel = data.channels.get_mut(&display).ok_or(FixtureError("unknown-channel"))?;
                if channel.task.is_some_and(|value| value != task) {
                    return Err(FixtureError("channel-task-changed"));
                }
                channel.task = Some(task);
                Ok(())
            })
        }
        pub fn unregister_task(&self, display: DisplayId) -> Result<(), FixtureError> {
            self.backend.perform(Point::Destroy, display, |data| {
                data.channels.remove(&display).ok_or(FixtureError("unknown-channel"))?;
                Ok(())
            })
        }
        pub fn request_activation(&self, display: DisplayId) -> Result<(), FixtureError> {
            self.backend.perform(Point::Activate, display, |data| {
                if !data.channels.contains_key(&display) {
                    return Err(FixtureError("unknown-channel"));
                }
                Ok(())
            })
        }
    }
}
pub mod service {
    use super::*;
    #[derive(Clone)]
    pub struct ComposerLifecycle { backend: Backend }
    impl ComposerLifecycle {
        pub fn fixture(backend: Backend) -> Self { Self { backend } }
        pub fn stage_task(&self, reservation: ReservedTaskWindowSpec) -> Result<(), FixtureError> {
            self.backend.perform(Point::Stage, reservation.display, |data| {
                if data.windows.contains_key(&reservation.display) {
                    return Err(FixtureError("duplicate-window"));
                }
                data.windows.insert(reservation.display, Window { package: reservation.package, task: None });
                Ok(())
            })
        }
        fn bind(&self, display: DisplayId, task: TaskId) -> Result<TaskWindowSpec, FixtureError> {
            self.backend.perform(Point::ComposerBind, display, |data| {
                if data.windows.iter().any(|(id, value)| *id != display && value.task == Some(task)) {
                    return Err(FixtureError("duplicate-window-task"));
                }
                let window = data.windows.get_mut(&display).ok_or(FixtureError("unknown-window"))?;
                if window.task.is_some_and(|value| value != task) {
                    return Err(FixtureError("window-task-changed"));
                }
                window.task = Some(task);
                Ok(TaskWindowSpec { task, display, package: window.package.clone() })
            })
        }
        pub fn bind_task(&self, display: DisplayId, task: TaskId) -> Result<TaskWindowSpec, FixtureError> {
            self.bind(display, task)
        }
        pub fn bind_direct_task(&self, display: DisplayId, task: TaskId) -> Result<TaskWindowSpec, FixtureError> {
            self.bind(display, task)
        }
        pub fn remove_display(&self, display: DisplayId) -> Result<Option<TaskWindowSpec>, FixtureError> {
            self.backend.perform(Point::Remove, display, |data| {
                let window = data.windows.remove(&display).ok_or(FixtureError("unknown-window"))?;
                Ok(window.task.map(|task| TaskWindowSpec { task, display, package: window.package }))
            })
        }
    }
}

            let weak = Arc::downgrade(&coordinator);
            io.configure_with(Some(Arc::new(move |object| {

            self.coordinator.register_direct_task(TASK, PACKAGE.to_owned(), ANDROID_DISPLAY)

            assert!(!state.direct_android_displays.contains_key(&object));

            drop(state);

            assert!(!self.io.has_window(display));
        }
        fn last_retired(&self) -> TaskObjectId {
            let state = self.coordinator.state.0.lock().unwrap();
            assert_eq!(state.retired.len(), 1);
